title: SA/196/2019 of SHOORVEER SINGH CHAUHAN Vs MAHANT SHRI BHOLAGIRI

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Second Appeal No. 196 of 2019
Shoorveer Singh Chauhan and Others
 ...Defendants/Appellants
Vs.
Mahant Shri Bholagiri
...Plaintiffs/Respondent
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for the appellants.
Mr. A.K. Sharma, Advocate for the respondent.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J (Oral)
The defendants (appellants herein) feeling themselves to
be aggrieved against the judgment dated 31.08.2017, as rendered by
the Civil Judge (S.D.), Vikasnagar, District Dehradun, in Original Suit
No. 598 of 2008 'Mahant Shri Bhola Giri Ji Maharaj vs. Sri Shoorveer
Singh Chauhan and Others', as well as, against the judgment dated
11.09.2019 passed by the Court of Additional District Judge,
Vikasnagar, District Dehradun, in Civil Appeal No. 15 of 2017 'Sri
Shoorveer Singh Chauhan and Others vs. Mahant Shri Bhola Giri Ji
Maharaj' has preferred this present second appeal.
2. Though apparently this second appeal seems to be
foundationed on a concurrent finding of facts, the only argument,
which has been extended by the learned counsel for the
defendants/appellants is based upon the substantial question of law
'C', which has been framed in the memorandum of appeal, which has
been attracted to be answered by this Court. Substantial question of
law 'C' as framed in the memorandum of appeal is quoted hereunder:
 "C. Whether the contents of an ex parte report of
survey Lekhpal without having any statutory backing and
without being proved before the Courts below in
accordance with the provisions with of the evidence act
could have any evidentiary value with regard to the facts
reported therein."
3. A short fact in order to answer the aforesaid substantial
question of law 'C' as involved in this case is that, even prior to the

2
institution of the Suit by the plaintiff/respondent on 21.11.2008. The
plaintiff (respondent herein) had filed an application before the Sub-Divisional Magistrate on 07.08.2008, which finds place on record as
paper No. 12A, on which in compliance of the S.D.M.'s order the
Sub-Divisional Magistrate has called a report, on which the report has
been submitted by the Lekhpal on 12.08.2008, i.e. Paper No. 12B, but
unfortunately and for the reasons undisclosed as it would be reflected
from the judgments under challenge itself that the said report of the
Lekhpal dated 12.08.2008, which has constituted as to be a reason for
answering issue no. 1 as well as issue no. 8 and also issue nos. 2, 4, 5
and 12, particularly, a reference may be had to the Trial Court's
judgment as recorded in paragraph-19, 29 and 40. The address made
by the Trial Court while recording its finding is based upon the report
of Lekhpal dated 12.08.2008, i.e. paper No. 12B.
4. The argument of the learned counsel for the
defendant/appellant is that though the said report Paper No. 12B and
the application constituted as to be the document on record by the
plaintiff/respondent and was even marked as paper numbers, but the
said documents, i.e. the report dated 12.08.2008, which have been
taken as to be the basis for deciding the controversy as raised by the
plaintiff/respondent to support his relief in the Suit, the same was not
made as an exhibit in view of the law as provided under Order 13
Rule 4 to be read with General Rules Civil. Order 13 Rule 4 of CPC is
quoted hereunder:
"Endorsements on documents admitted in evidence
(1) Subject to the provisions of the next following sub-rule,
there shall be endorsed on every document which has been
admitted in evidence in the suit the following particulars,
namely:-
 (a) the number and title of the suit,
 (b) the name of the person producing the document,
 (c) the date on which it was produced, and
 (d) a statement of its having been so admitted, and
the endorsement shall be signed or initialed by the
Judge.
(2) Where a document so admitted is an entry in a book,
account or record, and a copy thereof has been substituted for
the original under the next following rule, the particulars

3
aforesaid shall be endorsed on the copy and the endorsement
thereon shall be signed or initialled by the Judge."
5. It contemplates that merely the placing of a document on
record would not suffice the purpose, that the said document would be
read in evidence. Reading of a document in evidence would only be
based upon when the said document is marked as exhibit under Order
13 Rule 4, and after marking it as exhibit to be considered in
evidence, an opportunity is provided to the adversary to file his
rebuttal, and until and unless the said process is completed the said
document cannot be read in evidence for deciding the issues
materially affecting the rights of the parties to the proceedings.
6. This aspect as sought to be argued in the light of the
substantial question of law framed by the learned counsel for the
defendants/appellants by pressing substantial question 'C'. The
caveator was called upon to address on the issue as argued he has
more or less principally accepted that as far as the document paper
No. 12ga is concerned, which is the report of Lekhpal dated
12.08.2008 was not marked as an exhibit and hence under the
provisions contained under Order 13 Rule 4, and if that be the
situation the judgment rendered by the Trial Court and ultimately by
the Appellate Court too would be vitiated, as based upon the
appreciation of a document, which was not taken on record as an
exhibit in the proceedings before the court below.
7. Based with such procedural catastrophe, learned counsel
for the respondent principally admitted the said procedural anomaly
has committed by the Trial Court and later affirmed by the Appellate
Court without venturing in the said aspect of admissibility of
document, without marking as an exhibit and, hence, he has made a
request that the said mistake since it is not curable at a second
appellate stage, the matter may be remanded to the Trial Court for its
reconsideration after marking the report dated 12.08.2008, i.e. paper
No. 12B as an exhibit and after complying with the procedure

4
contemplated under Order 13 Rule 4, the matter may be directed to be
re-decided by the Trial Court.
8. In that view of the matter with the consensus of the
counsel for the parties, the present second appeal is allowed. The
impugned judgments are quashed. The matter is remanded back to the
Trial Court with a direction that whatsoever documents, which are on
record and if it is required to be read in evidence, they should be
marked as an exhibit. The defendants/appellants should be granted an
opportunity to file his rebuttal to those documents, and after providing
an opportunity of rebuttal, the adjudication of the Suit may be made
on its own merit.
9. Subject to above, the second appeal is allowed and the
matter is remanded back for fresh decision.
10. However, there would be no order as to cost.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 04.12.2019
Pooja
